_meta.name: MASQUE extraction development set
_meta.provenance: AUTHORED — written by hand to probe known failure modes. NOT openFDA, NOT FAERS, NOT patient data. Numbers computed on this set are development figures for guiding rule changes; they are NOT validation results and must not be reported as extraction performance on real narratives.
_meta.labelling: Single author, no adjudication. A real benchmark needs >=2 independent annotators with an inter-annotator agreement statistic; that is a stated gap, not an oversight.

registers.encounter: patient speech in clinic, first person
registers.narrative: third-person clinical prose, approximating a FAERS narrative

revisionLog: 0.2.0 — three labels corrected after the first benchmark run disagreed with them and the extractor turned out to be right. Recorded rather than silently amended: a gold set edited to match its system is not a gold set, so every change is listed with its reason.

cases.text: Bright lights make it so much worse, and I feel queasy the whole time.
It's been going on for over a year now and I've seen three doctors about it.
I had two rounds of antibiotics and a course of prednisone, nothing held.
The CT was normal and they said everything looked fine.
Grocery store aisles set it off, all those busy shelves.
My ear feels full and there's ringing when it happens.
The spinning lasts about two hours each time.
The dizziness only lasts a few seconds, then it passes.
I get vertigo that goes on for days at a stretch.
They told me it was probably stress and anxiety.
I've lost count of how many of these spells I've had.
My spells come with a headache most of the time.
cases.note: Corrected during benchmarking: the original label omitted m_head. 'Spells come with a headache' is a headache report, and the extractor was right.

cases.text: The scan showed mucosal thickening while I was flaring.
I can't smell anything anymore, even between the bad spells.
Thick green mucus every time it flares up.
My hearing test showed it drops during the spells.
I get deep ear pain but the ear looks fine every time.
Dry eyes, dry mouth, and I go lightheaded when I stand.
No nausea at all, but the light sensitivity is awful.
I don't get any aura, no spots or zigzags.
There's no ringing and my ears don't feel full.
I've never had sinus surgery.
Denies photophobia and phonophobia.
Patient is negative for nausea during episodes.
It's not the weather, I checked — it's when I skip meals.
probes: negation scope — negated cue, unnegated synonym in same sentence

cases.text: My mother gets migraines but I've never had one.
My sister is the one who gets the aura, not me.
Migraines run in the family on my dad's side.
probes: third-party attribution — family history IS the finding

cases.text: I used to get auras as a teenager but not for twenty years.
I had sinus surgery years ago and it did help for a while.
probes: historical — a past procedure is still a true finding

cases.text: The ringing is only in one ear, always the left.
cases.note: Corrected during benchmarking: ringing is a v_aural finding as well as a red flag. Original label listed only the flag.

cases.text: No, I've never had double vision or anything like that.
cases.note: Expected 'false positive' on a plain reading. It is the intended behaviour: capture may raise a flag, never clear one.
probes: red flag — denial must STILL raise

cases.text: It was the worst headache of my life, came on in seconds.
cases.note: Corrected during benchmarking: the original label omitted m_head.

cases.text: There's a whooshing that goes with my heartbeat.
The patient reported recurrent facial pressure with associated photophobia and nausea.
Symptoms reportedly began following a viral upper respiratory illness.
Episodes of vertigo lasting several hours were described.
Computed tomography of the sinuses demonstrated no acute abnormality.
The reporter noted the patient had undergone functional endoscopic sinus surgery without benefit.
Tinnitus was described as unilateral and pulsatile.
I work as a driving instructor, so I'm in the car all day.
We talked about the weather in the waiting room.
cases.note: Labelled as a capture because the rule genuinely fires. Kept in the set so the cost of the broad 'weather' cue stays visible.
probes: distractor — expected FP, vocabulary is too broad

cases.text: Everything's been fine since the last visit.
I take amoxicillin for my teeth sometimes.
probes: distractor — expected FP, no indication scoping
